articles.title: Cómo liberar espacio en Google Fotos, Drive y Gmail sin pagar y evitar que la cuenta deje de recibir correos
articles.summary:
Cada cuenta personal de Google incluye hasta 15 GB gratis que se reparten entre Gmail, Drive y Fotos. Al agotarse, deja de recibir correos y de guardar fotos. La ayuda oficial de la compañía detalla cómo recuperar espacio sin contratar un plan de pago.
Primero conviene saber qué ocupa lugar. Según la página de ayuda sobre el almacenamiento, cuentan los mensajes y adjuntos de Gmail (incluidas las carpetas de spam y papelera), los archivos de Drive, las copias de seguridad de fotos y videos en calidad original y las copias de seguridad de WhatsApp en Android.
Qué pasa si se supera el límite también está documentado. Gmail puede dejar de enviar y recibir mensajes, y los que lleguen se devuelven al remitente. Drive restringe la mayoría de las acciones, salvo descargar y eliminar, y Google Fotos deja de guardar copias nuevas.
Primero, vaciar la papelera y el spam
Para Google, la forma más rápida de recuperar espacio es vaciar la papelera y la carpeta de spam. Los elementos que están ahí siguen contando para el límite hasta que se borran de forma permanente. Lo mismo vale para la papelera de Drive y la de Fotos.
En Gmail, desde una computadora, se marca la casilla de cada mensaje que sobra y se pulsa Eliminar. Después se usa la opción Vaciar la papelera ahora. Si se borra mucho de golpe, el contador puede tardar entre 48 y 72 horas en reflejar el cambio, advierte la ayuda de Google. Un aviso de la propia ayuda: lo que se elimina de la papelera no se puede recuperar. Quien dude, pue…

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: SAP Confirms Cyberattack, Source Code Reportedly Compromised
articles.summary:
Enterprise software giant SAP has confirmed it is investigating a cybersecurity incident following reports that threat actors targeted its development infrastructure.
German publication Der Spiegel [paywalled] broke the news on Thursday, citing SAP insiders and an internal notification sent to employees.
SAP told SecurityWeek that it had detected suspicious activity and implemented measures to protect customers and secure its services. The German company did not disclose details of the attack.
“Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data,” SAP told SecurityWeek.
German news agency DPA reviewed internal SAP communications that revealed the suspicious activity had been identified within GitHub.
According to an insider cited by Der Spiegel, the hackers obtained SAP employees’ authentication tokens, enabling them to copy and alter source code stored on GitHub.
SAP publishes developer tools, sample applications, and open source projects on GitHub. It’s unclear whether the threat actor accessed any proprietary code.
Separately, Handelsblatt reported that SAP’s emergency security measures have affected numerous teams. The software giant has reportedly replaced signing keys, limited access to GitHub, and suspended automated development operations.
None of the reports indicate that tampered code was incorporated into software delivered to SAP customers.

articles.title: Kioxia Announces GP2 Series SSD with Over 18 Million Random Read IOPS
articles.summary:
Kioxia is introducing the GP2 Series SSD, and the standout number is more than 18 million random read IOPS at a 512-byte block size. I think we actually saw a precursor to this drive a few weeks ago. 18M IOPS is nearly double the performance of the GP1 Series Kioxia showed in August at FMS. The new drive is designed for PCIe 6.0 and NVMe 2.3, and Kioxia says it is also expecting sequential read throughput of up to 28GB/s, enough to saturate a PCIe 6.0 x4 link.
Kioxia GP2 Series Launched
The GP series is designed for a specific role in AI systems. Instead of adding more expensive HBM or DRAM to a GPU system, operators can use these NAND-based drives to create a flash-based memory tier the GPU can access directly. This lets the system handle larger datasets at a lower cost. Whenever you try to replace DRAM with NAND, endurance becomes a question. At 50DWPD, the GP2 is a step above many of the common capacity-focused drives.

|---|---|
| Interface | PCIe 6.0 / NVMe 2.3 | 
| Flash Memory | Kioxia XL-FLASH generation 3 | 
| Random Read Performance | More than 18 million IOPS at 512-byte block size |

| Endurance | Up to 50 DWPD | 
| Form Factors Under Consideration | E1.S 9.5 mm and E3.S |

Pourtant, le roman de Tolkien règle la question en quelques lignes, tandis que les films de Peter Jackson ne s’y attardent pas beaucoup plus.

D’aucuns pourraient trouver cela curieux : après tout, la série se passe au Deuxième Âge, plusieurs millénaires avant les péripéties de Frodon et de ses camarades au Troisième Âge. Mais cela n’est guère surprenant lorsque l’on a à faire avec des êtres magiques et surnaturels – ce que sont fondamentalement les mages dans l’œuvre de Tolkien.

articles.title: The new iPad Mini is getting its first major discount for Black Friday
articles.summary:
We were big fans of Apple’s new iPad Mini when we reviewed it in early November, but its steep starting price of $699 was hard to swallow. Thankfully, the small tablet is already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. Right now, Amazon and Walmart are both selling the 2026 iPad Mini with Wi-Fi and 128GB of storage starting at $599 ($100 off), its lowest price to date.
The new iPad Mini is getting its first major discount for Black Friday
Apple’s most portable tablet offers a larger OLED screen and water resistance.
The new Mini is a notable upgrade over its predecessor, with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display that delivers deeper blacks and better contrast than the previous model’s 8.3-inch LCD. Despite the bigger screen, the tablet itself is smaller and lighter, making it easier to carry. Apple also added IP67 dust and water resistance, so you have less reason to worry about where you use it. As my colleague David Pierce noted in his review, that made a big difference in his day-to-day use; he felt more comfortable handing the Mini to his spill-prone toddler or keeping it nearby in the kitchen to follow recipes. He even took it into the shower to keep watching a football game.
The upgraded A20 Pro chip also made apps load faster and demanding games run better in Pierce’s testing, while battery life held steady at around nine hours of screentime. articles.title: Hackers norcoreanos usan plataformas cripto poco conocidas para lavar parte de los USD 6.300 millones robados a Binance
articles.summary:
Los lavadores de dinero que trabajan para Corea del Norte avanzan hacia el cobro de parte de las criptomonedas robadas en el hackeo de Binance. Según investigadores citados por la agencia Reuters, usan servicios poco conocidos que cambian unas monedas por otras y borran el rastro de los fondos.
Las autoridades de Estados Unidos atribuyen a hackers norcoreanos el robo del 29 de octubre, el mayor de la historia en criptomonedas. Reuters lo cifra en USD 6.300 millones; la firma de análisis Elliptic habla de USD 6.430 millones repartidos en 11 cadenas de bloques. Corea del Norte niega su participación.
Los emisores de las monedas congelaron o incautaron USD 2.850 millones, según la agencia de noticias. El resto sigue en circulación y es lo que ahora se intenta limpiar con operaciones automatizadas que, según Elliptic, abarcan más de 27.000 billeteras, 16 cadenas de bloques, unos 55 servicios y cerca de 90.000 transacciones.
THORChain y los USD 600 millones que pasaron por ahí
Uno de esos servicios es THORChain, una plataforma de intercambio que se define como descentralizada. Los investigadores de Chainalysis y Elliptic estiman que más de USD 600 millones del botín pasaron por ella. Elliptic advirtió que la cifra puede incluir fondos que cruzaron la plataforma más de una vez.

articles.title: Mozilla Partners with Mistral to Bring Open-Weight AI Models to Firefox Smart Window
articles.summary:
Mozilla, the non-profit organisation behind the Firefox browser, has announced a partnership with Paris-based Mistral AI to bring the French company's open-weight models into Firefox Smart Window, Mozilla's AI browsing assistant currently in beta.
The deal introduces Mistral Small 4 as a recommended model for Smart Window users in France, the United States and Canada, with rollouts planned for the United Kingdom and Germany later this year. It coincides with Smart Window's first expansion beyond North America and marks a deliberate attempt by Mozilla to resist the pattern of browser makers coupling tightly to a single American AI provider.
Smart Window, originally announced in November 2025 as "AI Window", operates as an optional window separate from regular browsing. It helps users make sense of complex searches, group related tabs, revisit pages they have seen before and carry work across sessions. Users decide when to use it, which model to use and what browsing context to share. Conversations are not stored on Mozilla's servers by default, and Mistral has agreed to zero data retention for the partnership.
Mistral Small 4 is a 119-billion-parameter model distributed on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 licence. Mozilla selected it after evaluating performance in the beta, with multilingual quality as a central criterion. Un mes con el iPhone Duo es vivir ‘Regreso al futuro’
El primer plegable de Apple está cambiando mi forma de usar el móvil. Es refinado y, de lejos, el iPhone más divertido y rompedor que he probado. También resulta desconcertante y cabe esperar mejoras importantes. ¿Merece la pena pagar ahora 2.339 euros por él?
El Duo debutó hace un mes con colas ante las Apple Store como no se veían desde hace mucho tiempo y con los pedidos agotados hasta principios de 2027. Aquel día, mientras aguardaba la llegada del que me había enviado Apple, leía las primeras impresiones de quienes ya lo habían recibido. Los más entusiastas lo definían como “el iPhone del futuro”. Uno de esos tópicos que hacen arquear las cejas más escépticas. Y lo cierto es que el estreno del primer teléfono plegable de Apple me invitaba a viajar a su pasado: la fecha escogida era exactamente el 25º aniversario del día en que Steve Jobs presentó el primer iPod.
Probar el nuevo iPhone plegable recuerda algunas de las sensaciones de aquel iPod original. Tiene algo de ese Regreso al futuro en el que Marty McFly retrocedía varias décadas en el tiempo. Hace 25 años, también recibí una unidad de prueba de aquel reproductor musical, entonces en otra redacción. Casi nadie allí sabía que existía el iPod —en 2001, Apple era un fabricante de ordenadores de nicho— y se lo puse en las manos a una amiga, diseñadora de aquel periódico: “¿Pero qué es esto?”, me dijo. Companies wanted people who knew how to coax the best answers from large language models (LLMs) by carefully wording instructions, supplying examples, and giving the systems personas or other context.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

articles.title: Conta de luz terá bandeira verde em dezembro; veja o que muda
articles.summary:
A conta de luz dos brasileiros continuará sem cobrança adicional em dezembro. A Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) manteve a bandeira tarifária verde para o último mês de 2026, indicando condições favoráveis para a geração de energia elétrica no país.
O anúncio foi feito nesta sexta-feira (27). Segundo a agência reguladora, o aumento das chuvas e a melhora nos níveis dos reservatórios contribuíram para condições mais favoráveis de geração pelas usinas hidrelétricas.
Com esse cenário, não será necessário ampliar o acionamento de usinas termelétricas, que possuem custos de produção mais elevados. Dezembro será o terceiro mês consecutivo sem cobrança adicional pelo sistema de bandeiras tarifárias.
Como ficaram as bandeiras tarifárias em 2026?
A manutenção da bandeira verde representa uma mudança em relação ao período entre maio e setembro, quando os consumidores brasileiros ficaram sob a bandeira amarela durante cinco meses consecutivos.
A bandeira verde voltou em outubro e foi mantida em novembro e dezembro.

articles.title: Hex Package Manager Warns of Potential Data Breach
articles.summary:
Hex, the package manager for Elixir and Erlang, fell victim to a cyberattack involving unauthorized access to its web servers.
The incident occurred on November 23, when the attackers exploited a vulnerability in hex.pm to execute commands. The attack was immediately blocked, and the underlying security defect was addressed within 20 minutes.
Between 18:16 and 18:29 UTC, the attacker sent 69 malicious requests, affecting six web servers. At 18:30, Hex replaced all hex.pm servers with patched versions rejecting the payload, and its firewall rule fully blocked the attacker’s traffic at 18:33.
“We found no evidence of unauthorized package modifications, database changes, or that the attacker maintained access to our systems,” the package manager explains.
According to Hex, potential access to database contents, such as email addresses, password hashes, API key hashes, sessions, second factor authentication secrets, and audit logs, cannot be ruled out.
While all the observed reads of private packages came from Hex servers, any read from a compromised server would appear legitimate, it says. Additionally, database and private documentation reads are not logged, hindering visibility into potential data exposure.
“The attacker’s commands could read the credentials our servers use, so we replaced them: the storage, CDN, email and database credentials, and the keys that sign sessions and access tokens. This logged everyone out of hex.pm and Hex clients,” Hex notes.

articles.title: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
articles.summary:
A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System (NFS) server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges.
Found by ANSSI's Jérémy Jean (who submitted a fix in August), the flaw has been dubbed NFS2ROOT by cybersecurity firm OpenSec, which shared a full remote-root exploit and a patch with the NFSD maintainers in late September.
The vulnerability has existed since Linux kernel version 3.16 (released in March 2014), and it stems from a heap buffer overflow weakness in the Linux NFS server (nfsd).
NFS2ROOT affects systems with a Linux kernel older than 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2, or 7.4-rc1 if nfsd (v4.1 or 4.2) is loaded and running and TCP port 2049 is reachable over the Internet.
Successful exploitation lets remote threat actors without privileges corrupt kernel memory and gain root access to vulnerable Linux servers exposed online through low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction.
In NFS2ROOT attacks, the threat actors can exploit this flaw by sending maliciously crafted requests that cause the NFS server to write data beyond an allocated memory buffer. This lets them read kernel memory, bypass KASLR (which protects kernel memory addresses), and place a callback that can execute a command in a released memory area.
When the attacker closes the NFS connection, the kernel executes the embedded command with root privileges, allowing the attacker to gain root control of the unpatched Linux server.

C’est un grand classique de la vie de bureau : un contrat revient par e-mail en fichier .docx avec la fameuse mention « quelques ajustements mineurs » dont tout le monde se méfie. 
Jusqu’ici, pour vérifier ce qui avait réellement bougé dans Google Docs, il fallait d’abord convertir le fichier Word au format Google avant de pouvoir le comparer à sa propre version. Google Drive se remplissait vite de copies baptisées « contrat_v3_final_VRAI », jusqu’à ne plus savoir laquelle faisait foi. Cette étape inutile vient enfin de disparaître.
Présent dans Google Docs depuis 2019, l’outil « Comparer les documents » ne savait confronter que deux fichiers au format maison.
Mais le 16 novembre, Google a annoncé sur son blog Workspace Updates qu’il acceptait désormais les fichiers .docx (le format standard de Word) tels quels. 
D’après l’éditeur, la nouveauté est déjà déployée pour tout le monde, aussi bien sur les offres payantes Workspace et Workspace Individual que sur les comptes Google gratuits, sans réglage particulier. Docs savait déjà ouvrir et modifier un fichier Word nativement, et la comparaison faisait partie des derniers trous dans la raquette. Google continue ainsi d’empiler ces petits gains de temps au quotidien, dans la lignée du menu qui s’ouvre en tapant « @ ».
    Pour aller plus loin
Tapez juste « @ » : cette nouvelle fonction cachée de Google Docs va complètement révolutionner la rédaction d’un document

articles.title: « Tant qu’on en tire encore quelque chose » : un économiste propose de vendre Volkswagen à la Chine
articles.summary:
Volkswagen traverse sa plus mauvaise passe depuis le Dieselgate. Le 29 octobre, le groupe a annoncé une perte d’exploitation de 5,9 milliards d’euros sur le troisième trimestre 2026, alors qu’il commence à appliquer le plan d’austérité le plus radical de son histoire. Forcément, la crise du groupe alimente les spéculations.
Moritz Schularick, président de l’Institut de Kiel pour l’économie mondiale (IfW), en a avancé une pour le moins radicale ce mardi 24 novembre. À Berlin, lors d’une conférence sur l’industrie organisée par le ministère fédéral de l’Économie, le BDI (l’organisation patronale de l’industrie) et le syndicat IG Metall, il a suggéré de vendre aux Chinois « un certain groupe à Wolfsburg » (on se demande bien lequel), « tant qu’on peut encore en tirer quelque chose ». Selon le Handelsblatt, il estimait que ce ne serait « pas une mauvaise idée ».
Une manière de conserver la valeur ajoutée en Allemagne, vraiment ?
Pour l’économiste, ce qui compte, c’est que « la valeur ajoutée et la production restent ici ». « À qui appartient la production au bout du compte, c’est secondaire », a-t-il ajouté. Selon le Handelsblatt, ses propos ont fait murmurer la salle, d’autant que Michael Jansen, qui dirige la représentation de Volkswagen à Berlin, était dans le public.
Moritz Schularick estime que l’Allemagne est désormais un « pays en développement » face à la Chine sur ce marché. Il veut donc que l’Europe laisse entrer les voitures chinoises, mais qu’elle pousse leurs fabrica…

articles.title: Linux : une faille critique vieille de 12 ans permet de prendre le contrôle de serveurs, y compris de NAS, sans même s'authentifier
articles.summary:
Présente dans le noyau Linux depuis 2014, une vulnérabilité critique permet à des pirates de prendre le contrôle à distance de serveurs de fichiers sans disposer du moindre compte sur les machines ciblées. Découverte par un chercheur de l'ANSSI, la faille a depuis été exploitée en laboratoire par une intelligence artificielle.
Après Copy Fail, Dirty Frag et Fragnesia, NFS2ROOT vient gonfler la liste déjà longue des failles d'élévation de privilèges découvertes cette année dans le noyau Linux. Mais là où les précédentes nécessitaient que les pirates disposent déjà d'un accès au système, cette nouvelle vulnérabilité, référencée CVE-2026-99362 (CVSS 9,8/10), peut être exploitée à distance, sans authentification préalable.

Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.

- Source:

- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.

Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. articles.title: 100,000 Potentially Impacted by Colorado Data Breach
articles.summary:
The Colorado Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT) has disclosed a data breach impacting data that residents uploaded to the myColorado application.
Colorado’s official mobile application, myColorado is used for digital identification, state services, and document storage. It has approximately 2.1 million users.
OIT took the application offline last week, after identifying unauthorized access to platform data, and immediately initiated incident response and an investigation into the incident.
One week after the outage began, OIT said it discovered the incident after the attackers triggered the automated threat detection systems deployed within its Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment.
The investigation has determined that the attackers accessed documents stored within the ‘myCards and Documents’ section of the application, which includes user-uploaded data, such as PDF files and photos of government IDs, vehicle registrations, and insurance cards.
According to Colorado, approximately 100,000 individuals might have been affected, but no payment information was accessed.
“Staff are working around the clock to match the inappropriately accessed documents to individual users. As that matching continues, OIT will further refine estimates on the number of people whose data was involved,” Colorado said.
The myColorado application remains offline and OIT has not announced a restoration date. The state expects to start sending direct notifications to the affected individu…

articles.title: La Unión Europea podría votar el 15 de diciembre si autoriza el sistema de conducción asistida de Tesla
articles.summary:
El comité de expertos de los países de la Unión Europea que regula los vehículos podría votar el 15 de diciembre si autoriza en todo el bloque el sistema de asistencia a la conducción de Tesla, que la empresa vendía como “Full Self-Driving”. Según el borrador de la agenda, será la primera vez que se incluye una votación.
El Comité Técnico de Vehículos de Motor (TCMV, por sus siglas en inglés) se reúne en Bruselas de 10:00 a 15:00. El punto 4, entre las 10:40 y las 11:10, trata el proyecto de decisión que autorizaría a los Países Bajos a conceder la homologación europea del sistema.
El sistema se llama ahora “Tesla Assisted Driving” y el punto lleva la indicación “posible votación”, según el sitio especializado Not an FSD Tracker, que cita el registro de comitología de la Comisión Europea.
“Posible” significa que el comité puede votar ese día, pero no está obligado. El borrador de agenda, fechado el 24 de noviembre, todavía puede cambiar. Not an FSD Tracker indica que la agencia Reuters informó el 26 de noviembre que la Comisión planteó de forma explícita la opción de votar, algo que no había ocurrido en reuniones anteriores. La reunión estaba prevista para el 1 de diciembre. Un portavoz de la Comisión Europea confirmó el nuevo día a Reuters y nadie dio una razón pública del cambio.
Se necesitan 15 países y el 65% de la población
Una aprobación en todo el bloque exige el voto favorable de al menos 15 de los 27 Estados miembros, que representen como mínimo el 65% de la població…

"Affected devices might stop unexpectedly with stop error 0x139 (KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE) when a route timer expires. This issue affects some Windows Server 2025 devices after installing the November 2026 Windows security hotpatch update."
This emergency non-security update is now rolling out to affected Windows Server 2025 devices enrolled in hotpatch updates through Windows Update.

Además, tanto los cocineros como los nutricionistas coinciden en que con este zumo el resultado será más jugoso y saludable que con aceite.
Características del salmón. El salmón un pescado graso con las propiedades típicas de los pescados azules: 12 gramos de lípidos por cada 100 gramos de porción comestible, una cantidad parecida a la de los atunes o los reos, y aportes importantes de ácidos grasos monoinsaturados y poliinsaturados, entre ellos omega 3 y omega 6. Además, también es una rica fuente de proteínas.
Lo que vas a necesitar. Para la receta hacen falta dos lomos de salmón, 200 mililitros de zumo de naranja y un par de rodajas de la misma fruta, a los que se suman una cucharada de salsa de soja, otra de miel, una cucharadita de jengibre rallado, un diente de ajo, una cucharada de aceite, sal y pimienta. Al final también se utiliza cebollino para decorar, aunque no aparece en la lista de ingredientes.
Primero, la salsa. Pero antes de encender el fuego toca preparar la salsa: se ralla la piel de la naranja, se exprime para sacar el zumo y se ralla también el jengibre, y después se mezcla todo con la miel y la soja hasta que quede homogéneo. Por último, se pica el diente de ajo y se añade a la mezcla.

articles.title: Série noire aux États-Unis : des pirates se sont infiltrés dans Cloud One, la plateforme cloud géante de l’US Air Force
articles.summary:
L’intrusion dans le cloud de l’armée de l’air américaine a été repérée il y a environ un mois, au cours de travaux de mise à niveau du système, selon deux des sources de Reuters.
D’après une dépêche du 27 novembre de l’agence de presse Reuters, qui s’appuie sur cinq sources anonymes, des pirates ont réussi à pénétrer Cloud One, la plateforme cloud phare de l’US Air Force.
Lancée en 2017 avec Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle et Alphabet, elle fait tourner des dizaines d’applications, de la paie à la logistique, mais aussi des outils sensibles comme celui qui rassemble les données radar de défense aérienne de toute l’Amérique du Nord.
Les pirates ont atteint le cœur de la plateforme
Interrogée par Reuters, l’Air Force a seulement répondu qu’elle ne commentait pas « la posture de sécurité, les vulnérabilités ou l’état opérationnel » de ses réseaux. Les détails recueillis par l’agence de presse restent maigres. On ne sait ni qui sont les pirates, ni jusqu’où ils sont allés, ni si des données ont été volées.
D’après une des sources de Reuters, les attaquants ont exploité une vulnérabilité logicielle pour atteindre le « control plane », la couche d’administration du cloud, qu’elle compare à une télécommande universelle. Un tel accès permettrait en théorie de consulter l’état opérationnel des avions militaires ou de suivre les mouvements de pièces détachées, sans que l’on sache si les pirates l’ont fait.

The software company reportedly asked all employees to keep the project details confidential.

Ce second numéro pourra être enregistré comme deuxième compte WhatsApp grâce au multi-compte, ou rester cantonné à la connexion. Vercel’s CEO thinks the next big AI speedup won’t come from smarter models
Some of the biggest gains in AI performance over the past year have come from improvements to the harness, not the model itself. But Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch believes that as models become more capable, some implementation details developers have spent months refining will become less visible, and the infrastructure that executes agents will become more important.
“As AI gets smarter, implementation details blur away: permissions, code diffs, commands, tool calls. … The harness itself blurs away.”
“As AI gets smarter, implementation details blur away: permissions, code diffs, commands, tool calls,” Rauch wrote in a post on X. “The harness itself blurs away.”
Rauch doesn’t expect the harness to disappear entirely. He sees its role shifting toward executing agents and preserving their state.
Vercel offered a glimpse of what that architecture could look like on Wednesday with the release of Workflow SDK 5.8, which introduces a rebuilt execution engine that substantially reduces the infrastructure overhead associated with running durable agents.
Latency between the model calls
Inference speed accounts for only part of an agent’s total execution time. Much of the latency can accumulate in the infrastructure that handles work between model calls.
Vercel’s new execution engine addresses that overhead through speculative execution of retryable workflow steps.

articles.title: Fake Roblox cheats are delivering password-stealing malware to family computers
articles.summary:
The takeaway: Cybercriminals are hiding infostealer malware inside fake Roblox cheat tools, and a child who downloads one may hand over a parent's banking logins and work email along with the game account. A Cybernews analysis of search data found more than 22 million cheat-related Roblox searches between 2018 and 2026, which gives attackers a very large pool of potential victims. Bitdefender and SOC Prime have each documented campaigns this year in which the counterfeit tools did their advertised job while quietly stealing data.
Cybernews measured demand by tracking how often people searched for cheat-related terms on Google and Yandex. It covered 17 games in 184 countries, using the most popular phrases in English and in local languages. Roblox accounted for over half of all the cheat searches. Adjusted for audience size, the platform drew 482 cheat searches per 1,000 players, ahead of Valorant at 434 and Call of Duty: Warzone at 408. Minecraft came in at 74.
The appeal of a free shortcut is easy to see. Roblox costs nothing to download, but experiences inside it can put top weapons, VIP perks and rare items behind paywalls of roughly $5 to $50.
Roblox reported average spending of $12.29 per player in the third quarter of 2026, when it counted 138 million daily active users. Children without access to a credit card look to YouTube and Google for scripts that automate the grinding, and that is where the trouble starts.

articles.title: Cómo restaurar la configuración de Google Chrome y liberar memoria RAM en casa
articles.summary:
Un ajuste de Google Chrome vinculado a Gemini puede estar consumiendo memoria RAM de tu computadora incluso después de cerrar el navegador. El hallazgo partió de un usuario que detectó, a través del Administrador de Tareas de Windows, que varios procesos de chrome.exe seguían activos tras pulsar la X de la ventana.
El caso, documentado en una publicación de Reddit, muestra que esos procesos residuales llegaban a ocupar entre 300 MB y 700 MB de RAM. La causa no estaba en extensiones ni en configuraciones habituales, sino en una función de inteligencia artificial integrada al navegador.
Por qué Chrome sigue activo después de cerrarse
El comportamiento no responde a un fallo aislado. Chrome mantiene ciertos componentes cargados en memoria para que el asistente Gemini pueda responder de inmediato cuando el usuario lo invoca, incluso con el navegador minimizado o cerrado.
Quien reportó el problema explicó que probó borrar caché y cookies, deshabilitar todos los complementos, eliminar aplicaciones web instaladas, resetear la configuración y desactivar la aceleración por hardware, el precargado de páginas y la inteligencia artificial en el dispositivo. Ninguna de esas acciones resolvió el consumo.
La pista definitiva llegó al crear un perfil nuevo sin sesión iniciada: ese perfil cerraba Chrome por completo, sin procesos residuales. Eso permitió aislar el origen del problema en una configuración asociada específicamente al perfil con sesión activa.

Last week, Drupal patched a remote code execution (RCE) flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-132165 / Fail2Install) that lets anonymous users take over vulnerable sites by abusing the Drupal installer.
While the security issue wasn't initially flagged as being abused in the wild, an update to the original security advisory warned that threat actors began exploiting it one day after patches were released.
The new security issue (CVE-2026-136716), patched one week later, addresses attack vectors that were left unpatched and also lets attackers hijack vulnerable Drupal sites.

More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. The latest to join the trend is Volvo, which is training humanoid robots at its manufacturing plant in Ghent, Belgium. As is always the case when machines enter the workplace, Volvo claims the idea is for the robots to take on some of the more repetitive and physically demanding jobs, but there's always the specter of replacement in instances like these.
Ghent is the first Volvo plant to try the AEON humanoids, built by Swedish technology group Hexagon. Volvo employees show the robots how to place components precisely into two fixtures, and the machines learn by copying them. Once they can do that reliably, the team will teach them to handle several parts, move around the production area, and work with the plant's automated equipment.
AEON stands about 5 feet 5 inches tall, weighs 132 pounds, and can carry 22 pounds. One decidedly unhuman feature is the set of wheels that can propel it across the factory floor at just over 5 mph. The appeal for Volvo is that AEON can move between workstations designed for people, something a robotic arm bolted to the floor would struggle to do, obviously.
More robots are due in Ghent for a larger pilot in the first half of 2027. Volvo wants them working on the production line by the middle of the year, though it hasn't said how many will join the workforce or what that might mean for the people currently doing those jobs.

articles.title: Engineering Reliable Telematics from Smartphone Sensors
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Smartphone GPS, motion sensors, and vehicle interfaces can each report valid measurements that produce incorrect results when combined without accounting for timing and coordinate frames.
- Preserve raw observations and their provenance before synchronizing, transforming, or normalizing them.
- Introduce a quality gate that determines whether telemetry is suitable for a particular decision instead of forcing every observation into a definitive result.
- Design for real-world conditions, including delayed GPS updates, phone movement, background interruptions, and intermittent connectivity.
- Monitor data quality alongside conventional application and infrastructure metrics because a functioning pipeline can still produce unreliable driving events.
Why this matters: the phone is not the vehicle
A smartphone can provide a surprising amount of information about a journey, including GPS estimates location and speed, accelerometers measure motion along the device's axes, gyroscopes capture rotation, and others. A connected vehicle may expose additional signals, such as speed, engine state, or diagnostic information.
Combining these sources creates opportunities for fleet monitoring, usage-based insurance, driving-behavior analysis, trip reconstruction, and connected mobility services.
However, having more sensors does not automatically produce better telemetry.

articles.title: Microsoft removes WSUS server role in Windows Server 2028
articles.summary:
Microsoft will remove the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system.
Introduced in 2005 as Software Update Services (SUS), WSUS (Windows Server Update Services) lets IT administrators manage and distribute updates for Microsoft products across corporate networks with many Windows devices.
It gives admins centralized control over the updates, rather than having each device download them individually from Microsoft's servers.
Microsoft has officially deprecated WSUS in September 2024, but said that it still plans to maintain functionality and continue publishing updates through the channel. The change affects enterprise environments that rely on WSUS to manage updates delivered to many devices but does not impact home users or those using Microsoft Configuration Manager.
In a recently updated support document, Microsoft went even further and confirmed that Windows Server 2028 removes the WSUS server role altogether.
"WSUS remains available and supported in earlier Windows Server releases, including Windows Server 2025, for the duration of each release's support lifecycle. You can continue to use WSUS on those releases to manage updates for supported Windows client and Windows Server releases, which includes updates to Windows Server 2028," it said.

articles.title: TV Hisense et pistage audio : voici le seul réglage qui coupe vraiment l'envoi de vos données

Pour le repérer, ce Britannique a dû déchiffrer le trafic réseau de sa propre télévision, un passe-temps de week-end peu banal. Vous ne trouvez pas ? On ne jugera pas.
Contrairement à ce qu’on pourrait craindre, le micro n’est pas en cause dans son analyse : le système est beaucoup plus discret, et il tourne dès la première configuration.
En coulisses, tout passe par un programme nommé HamService qui fonctionne en tâche de fond sur Vidaa, le système d’exploitation maison de Hisense. Il embarque un SDK (un bloc de code fourni par un tiers) de Nexxen dédié à l’ACR, la reconnaissance automatique de contenus : une technologie pensée pour identifier ce que vous regardez et revendre ces données.
Le téléviseur résume le son chaque quart de seconde en une empreinte de 72 bits, puis envoie toutes les 2,7 secondes les dix dernières lignes accompagnées de son identifiant fixe, de l’heure, de l’entrée utilisée et de l’application ouverte. Ce débit minuscule (270 bits par seconde, contre 128 000 pour l’audio d’origine) ne permet pas de réécouter votre salon, mais suffit largement à reconnaître un film ou une série. articles.title: Houston, we have a networking problem: Why NTT thinks space computing is the final frontier
articles.summary:
Houston, we have a networking problem: Why NTT thinks space computing is the final frontier
After cloud computing comes space computing, obviously, right? There’s a neat irony here: Real-world clouds can interfere with optical satellite links. Cloud cover (along with atmospheric turbulence) can block the laser-based connections between satellites and ground stations, limiting how much data can be brought down to the data center and cloud services waiting for it. In other words, cloud services on the ground can be held back by the weather they are named after.
Networking conglomerate NTT wants to enable a new era of communications above the clouds (literally) with a combined set of space computing and lunar infrastructure developments that draw heavily on its work in photonics and light-based computing.
The organization’s optical space communication infrastructure is now being aligned with technologies supporting observation and space datacenter creation. The company is also working on lunar surface communication and lunar energy transmission.
Our 88 constellations just got one louder
Today, the International Astronomical Union recognizes 88 constellations in the sky; the NTT C89 project was launched in 2024 to unify and scale the company’s space-related projects and create what it believes could be the 89th constellation.

articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.summary:
Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
- Date:
  November 16, 2026
- Source:
  University of Innsbruck
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.
- Share:
As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising new method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.
The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.

articles.title: Canadian password manager 1Password has been hacked
articles.summary:
Toronto-based password manager 1Password has revealed that it was the victim of a hack that compromised some customer data.
In a blog post this week, the company confirmed that a hacker was able to breach its system through an employee’s corporate GitHub account. From there, the hacker could access customer names and email addresses, as well as non-secret internal metadata about the account. However, 1Password says none of customers’ vault contents or passwords have been leaked.
The company says it’s since disabled the affected GitHub account, added tighter controls and detection tools, and brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate its efforts. It also reminds customers that 1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. It adds that suspicious activity can be reported by emailing support@1password.com.

Ripple effect: Ethical security researcher Jeremiah Fowler recently uncovered a massive unsecured database containing around two billion potentially compromised account credentials. A single database was apparently hosting several collections of account credentials from multiple security incidents, and anyone could download the data before the host decided to block access.
Fowler said that the database he discovered was neither protected by a password nor encrypted in any way. Around 2 billion credentials were just sitting there, waiting for someone to grab the data and use it to launch further attacks against users. The dataset included email addresses, logins and other user IDs, passwords, and more.
The researcher probed the online database by reviewing the neatly organized data, finding additional content types such as application credentials, browser passwords, cookies, session tokens, and other "identifiers." Fowler said that this was the largest collection of compromised accounts he had ever found. The dataset was more than 13 times bigger than an exposure he previously reported and included a lot more device-specific data for potential attackers to exploit.
The database was also noteworthy for how the plaintext data was organized in thousands of different folders, with some documents grouped by country-code top-level domain. Around 400,000 documents appeared to come from advanced malware threats, as they were stored in separate folders focused on individual victims.

articles.title: AWS Nitro Sandboxes give AI agents a place to run
articles.summary:
AWS Nitro Sandboxes give AI agents a place to run
A coding agent has written a script and wants to run it. The script may do exactly what the developer asked. The next decision, though, belongs to humans.
The team building the system has to answer a slew of questions: Where should that code run? What should it be able to reach once it starts?
The script doesn’t get a vote.
At the recent KubeCon + CloudNativeCon conference in Salt Lake City, The New Stack’s Frederic Lardinois asked AWS Senior Product Manager Mike Stefaniak what’s keeping more teams from running agents in production.
Stefaniak said he’s seen a handful of large customers commit in a big way. Many others are still figuring out security and identity. AWS Nitro Sandboxes, announced at the conference, address one part of that problem by giving developers an isolated place to run container workloads.
Keep the image, change where it runs
Stefaniak describes Nitro Sandboxes as a way to bring the isolation of the Nitro hypervisor to multiple workloads within one EC2 instance. Each sandbox draws CPU and memory from the parent instance.
“You don’t have to change your container image.”
On EKS Auto Mode or ECS Managed Instances, Stefaniak says, a runtime configuration tells AWS to place the workload in a sandbox.
“You don’t have to change your container image.”
That’s important to a developer with an existing build pipeline who wants to change how a workload runs without rebuilding the application around a new packaging mod…

Hala Mobility combines EV rentals, delivery jobs, and financial services for gig workers
Hyderabad-based startup Hala Mobility provides electric vehicles to delivery riders, connects them with delivery companies, and offers early-salary financing and accident insurance.
Delivery riders can cover 100 to 120 km a day, often on petrol vehicles that aren’t designed for such intensive use. Rising fuel prices add to their operating costs.
Electric vehicles (EVs) can reduce these expenses, and delivery companies are encouraging riders to make the switch. However, riders who cannot afford or access an EV have little choice but to continue using petrol vehicles.
Access to a vehicle is only part of the problem. Riders also need to know how far it can travel on a charge, where to charge it, and where to get it serviced. For companies managing large EV fleets, the challenges extend to monitoring battery health, battery swaps, energy consumption, and maintenance schedules.
Hyderabad-based Hala Mobility aims to address these gaps through an EV fleet-as-a-service and multi-modal shared mobility platform that allows riders and delivery companies to use EVs without purchasing them.
Through the Hala app, riders can rent, lease or finance vehicles. Hala was founded in 2019 by Srikanth Reddy Kalakonda, Founder and CEO, and Co-founder Snehith Reddy Meda.

articles.title: Your Firewall Isn't Enough: The Hidden Risk of Unmanaged VMs
articles.summary:
When discussing IT infrastructure security, the focus is usually on firewalls, EDR, backup, vulnerability management, and network segmentation. However, all of them are effective only under one condition — if the infrastructure itself is under control.
Incidents often begin not with the exploitation of a vulnerability or bypassing protection systems, but with shortcomings in basic infrastructure management. Every virtual machine, server, access, and IP address must have an owner, a lifetime, and a controlled path for creation and deletion.
When management processes are opaque, the infrastructure itself becomes a source of information security risks, and security tools have to operate over an unknown environment and merely contain the consequences.
This principle is equally critical for enterprise companies and service providers — regardless of whether the platform serves internal services, development teams, or external customers, a loss of control over administration can lead to the compromise of the entire environment.
Why Security Grows Out of Manageability
In modern IT infrastructure, hundreds of systems run on the same resources, and the environment itself is constantly changing — dozens of services are created, scaled, and deleted daily.
In such conditions, provisioning comes to the fore. Deploying a new virtual machine without a regulation and recording the owner leaves "forgotten" VMs in the environment. They do not receive updates, fall out of monitoring, and become …

Instalar cámaras de vigilancia en las zonas comunes de un edificio no es algo que pueda decidir un vecino por su cuenta, ni siquiera la comunidad de vecinos si no hay una votación con una mayoría concreta. Qué dice el artículo 17.3. Este apartado de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal incluye la vigilancia entre los servicios comunes de interés general y lo dice de esta manera: “El establecimiento o supresión de los servicios de portería, conserjería, vigilancia u otros servicios comunes de interés general, supongan o no modificación del título constitutivo o de los estatutos, requerirán el voto favorable de las tres quintas partes del total de los propietarios que, a su vez, representen las tres quintas partes de las cuotas de participación”.
Dos mayorías a la vez. Esto significa que la instalación tiene que aprobarse en la junta de propietarios y que el recuento se hace dos veces, por número de propietarios y por cuotas de participación. articles.title: España nunca ha tenido cuatro inviernos consecutivos sin una sola ola de frío. AEMET empieza a temer que sea algo inevitable (con todo lo que ello conlleva)
articles.summary:
El día de Reyes de 2026, el termómetro de Molina de Aragón bajó hasta los 14 grados bajo cero. Era el cénit de un periodo de cinco días que dejó esa zona del país unos 5 grados por debajo de lo habitual. Dos meses después, como suele hacer, la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET) repasó el invierno y llegó a la conclusión de que, con la información disponible, nada de lo que pasó en aquellos cinco días podía considerarse una ola de frío.
No dio la talla, no entró en la lista. Lo cual tampoco es raro, porque, en fin, la lista lleva sin tener nuevos miembros desde el 2 de marzo de 2023.
Eso quiere decir que llevamos tres inviernos completos sin una sola ola de frío. Nunca en toda la serie habíamos encadenado tres. Pero eso no es lo peor: lo peor es que el cuarto empieza el 1 de diciembre.
¿Qué es una ola de frío? Es curioso. Lo primero que deja claro el estudio de referencia de AEMET es que (históricamente) no ha existido una definición oficial. También que el término se usa con "una tendencia a exagerar". Por ello, la agencia eligió un criterio a posteriori y lo aplicó, invierno a invierno, hasta 1975.
A día de hoy, una 'ola de frío' tiene que cumplir tres condiciones a la vez: a) durar al menos tres días consecutivos en el que b) como mínimo el 10% de las estaciones c) registra mínimas por debajo de un umbral.
Como tenemos apenas 131 estaciones, repartidas por la Península y Baleares (Canarias queda fuera por lo suave de sus temperaturas), hacen falta 14.

articles.title: Recent Outages Have Economic Causes
articles.summary:
Recent Outages Have Economic Causes
This essay originally appeared in The Guardian. It’s an expanded version of the one I posted as “We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For.”
It’s been a bad week for our computerized infrastructure. We’ve seen outages at Microsoft, the FAA, a handful of banks, United Airlines, an unnamed classified NSA network, and Apple. People should be forgiven for suspecting a coordinated cyberattack, a common cause, or at least a conspiracy. But there is none.
The incidents are unrelated. They’re not the result of any cyberattack, coordinated or not. And, even more surprising, they don’t seem to be the result of AI. (We can’t say anything about the NSA; we’ll probably never know the details of that one.) It’s really just a series of unfortunate coincidences.
None of them should surprise, though. Our computerized infrastructure is both vulnerable and fragile.
Much of it is old and has been incrementally patched and upgraded over the decades. A surprising amount of it is maintained by hobbyists, without any recompense. There often aren’t good backup systems. And more and more of it is centralized, meaning that individual failures have cascading consequences across many different aspects of our lives and society.
A lot of our tech infrastructure just barely works. And when it fails, it can fail badly. It’s the very opposite of resilience.

articles.title: A 1950s elevator just sent a message through a brick wall using nothing but gravity
articles.summary:
What just happened? These days, nearly every wireless signal around us, from those carrying Wi-Fi to 5G, can be stopped by a thick enough wall or a metal box. Gravity is different, since no known material can block or shield it. Physicists in Australia have now used that quirk to send a short message through a brick wall. Weirdly, the transmitter was just an old elevator in their own building.
The elevator in question sits inside the University of Queensland's Parnell Building and dates back to the 1950s. It has a 1.8-metric-ton counterweight that moves the opposite way whenever the car travels between floors, so the team treated one position of that weight as a 0 and the other as a 1. Then they ran the elevator up and down to spell out a binary message.
Meanwhile, the receiver was an off-the-shelf gravimeter sitting in a bathroom next to the shaft, behind a brick wall. Each time the weight moved, gravity at the sensor changed by just five billionths of its normal strength. Still, it was enough for the team to decode a single, rather fitting word: "Gravity."
The catch is that the old elevator needs about 25 seconds just to shift the counterweight. So the setup managed only one bit per minute.
Spelling out "Gravity" in seven-bit ASCII took 49 bits, or nearly an hour of moving the elevator. Fans of Interstellar might remember Cooper pulling off something similar, using gravity to transmit Morse code onto his daughter's watch. But where his message crossed dimensions, this one o…

articles.title: Netflix Builds Quasar to Measure the Blast Radius of Library API Changes
articles.summary:
Netflix has developed Quasar, an internal tool that identifies which repositories use specific library API symbols, helping engineering teams assess the downstream impact of proposed changes before releasing them. The tool combines semantic code indexing with API comparisons to identify affected consumers, dependency versions, and relevant call sites across repositories.
The challenge extends beyond identifying whether an API change is incompatible. Compatibility tools can flag a removed method or changed signature, but they do not necessarily identify which applications call it. Dependency graphs show declared relationships rather than actual usage, while text searches can miss references involving inheritance, overloads, and generated code. Building every downstream consumer to validate a change can also be expensive.
Quasar architecture diagram showing the indexing and query workflow (Source: Netflix Blog Post)
Quasar indexes symbol definitions and references using the SCIP Code Intelligence Protocol, an open format for representing code relationships. Language-specific indexers submit data during CI builds, which Quasar stores in Amazon S3 as Parquet files and queries through Amazon Athena.

27,3 millions de kilomètres carrés. C’est la taille atteinte le 20 septembre 2026 par le trou de la couche d’ozone au-dessus de l’Antarctique, soit près de deux fois la superficie du continent glacé et 31 % de plus que la moyenne des vingt dernières années à la même période. Ces chiffres, communiqués par l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) le 26 novembre 2026, nous viennent du programme européen d’observation de la Terre Copernicus, et plus précisément de Sentinel-5P, un satellite chargé de surveiller l’état de l’atmosphère terrestre depuis 2017.
Ce trou est en réalité un appauvrissement de la couche d’ozone au-dessus de l’Antarctique, qui se forme chaque année au printemps austral, quand le froid extrême de la stratosphère polaire favorise la destruction de l’ozone. Le phénomène est saisonnier et dépend aussi du retour du soleil, mais il est d’abord provoqué par les activités humaines, et plus précisément par les CFC et autres gaz chlorés ou bromés longtemps utilisés dans les aérosols, les réfrigérateurs ou les climatiseurs. Voir l’un des plus grands trous en près d’un demi-siècle peut donc paraître inquiétant à première vue – pourtant, la situation n’est pas si simple, et surtout pas si catastrophique.

articles.title: La reflexión de Albert Einstein sobre las personas independientes: "La monotonía y la soledad de una vida tranquila estimulan la mente creativa"
articles.summary:
Albert Einstein tenía una propuesta bastante peculiar para los jóvenes que querían dedicarse a la ciencia: trabajar en un faro. No lo decía de broma. En octubre de 1933, durante una intervención en Londres, el físico defendió que algunos empleos tranquilos podían ser una buena alternativa para quienes necesitaban tiempo libre para investigar. Su preocupación era que muchos científicos estuvieran demasiado ocupados intentando ganarse la vida.
En aquella conferencia también habló de su propia experiencia viviendo apartado en el campo. Fue entonces cuando explicó que había comprobado cómo "la monotonía de una vida tranquila estimula la mente creativa". La frase, recuperada por OKDIARIO en un artículo sobre las personas independientes, resumía algo que Einstein valoraba especialmente: poder dedicar horas a pensar sin demasiadas interrupciones.
Por qué Einstein prefería un faro a una beca de investigación
El científico consideraba que trabajar en un faro podía dejar tiempo suficiente para estudiar matemáticas o filosofía. La idea tenía su lógica: en lugar de depender de una beca de investigación, un joven podría tener un empleo con el que mantenerse y reservar parte del día para desarrollar sus propios proyectos.
Einstein también cuestionó las dificultades que encontraban quienes recibían ayudas para investigar. A su juicio, la obligación de presentar resultados en periodos demasiado cortos podía perjudicar trabajos que necesitaban años de dedicación. Por eso pensaba que disponer …

Nigerian startup Omata AI has built a WhatsApp-native business operating system that helps small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) manage their day-to-day operations through simple conversations.
The flagship product of Autonomous Data Enterprise, a company founded in 2026 by Stanley Okafor, Omata AI lets merchants record sales, manage inventory, track customer balances and monitor business performance by sending WhatsApp messages. A connected dashboard gives them more oversight.
“Our vision is to make business management as easy as sending a WhatsApp message,” Okafor told Disrupt Africa. “For example, a trader can send a message such as, “I sold two bags of rice for NGN50,000”, and Omata AI can interpret the information, prepare a structured transaction and request the merchant’s approval before confirmation.”
Okafor said that many small businesses across Africa still rely on notebooks, memory and scattered WhatsApp chats to manage their records. Existing accounting, POS and inventory tools are often too complex or too costly for them.
“Rather than asking merchants to adapt to complicated software, we want business software to adapt to the way they already operate,” he said.
The startup’s main differentiator is what Okafor calls a “human-approval-first” architecture. Under this design, AI cannot change financial records without the business owner’s sign-off.

- Share:
Bladder cancer kills approximately 220,000 people worldwide each year, yet recognizing the disease early can be difficult. Its symptoms can resemble those of far less serious conditions, including kidney stones, allowing warning signs to go unnoticed.
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.
The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.

articles.title: Hunger strike outside Anthropic HQ enters third day as activist demands "AI might kill everyone" warning

Sounding off: A lot of people are worried about the development of RSI, or recursive self-improvement, and their concerns are understandable. It's the concept of an AI system improving its own capabilities, with each improved version becoming better at making further improvements. One activist is so against RSI that he's holding a hunger strike outside Anthropic's San Francisco HQ. In an update on his third day there, he said he could go without food for 40 days or more.
Elliot Callender listed eight conditions and said he'd end his protest if any one of them were met. One that Anthropic could meet on its own is to put a warning on every one of its products under the heading "AI might kill everyone," which, in fairness, it warned could happen in its IPO prospectus.
Callender wants the company to explain why AI systems given very different goals might still find it useful to do things like acquire more resources or avoid being shut down. He also wants it to explain how long researchers have been discussing the risk of human extinction and point users to the infamous incident in which an OpenAI agent compromised accounts across four services, including Hugging Face.
Some of his other conditions are even less likely to happen. Callender says he would leave if Anthropic halted all AI research, development, and training and put at least 80% of its cash and revenue toward lobbying for a bilateral AI treaty. The news: Vancouver-based Bluprint, which claims to be Canada’s only business accelerator focused exclusively on sustainable construction tech, announced the 20 Canadian startups participating in its latest cohort last week. This group includes cleantech, hardtech, and proptech companies developing advanced building materials, cleaner energy systems, and other products designed to boost construction productivity, slash costs, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Participants include Kamloops, BC-based kWattWorks, Vancouver’s Torch Labs, and Guelph, Ontario’s Hundred Year Materials, among others.
From the source: “Their technologies have the potential to address some of the industry’s most pressing challenges,” Gil Yaron, managing director of circular innovation with sustainable construction-focused non-profit Light House, said in a statement. articles.title: Limited Demand Visibility and Growing Supply Chain Caution Heighten Risk of DRAM Contract Price Declines in 2028
articles.summary:
Friday, November 27th 2026
Limited Demand Visibility and Growing Supply Chain Caution Heighten Risk of DRAM Contract Price Declines in 2028
TrendForce's latest memory industry findings indicate that supply chain participants have been reassessing their production and sales plans for 2027 and 2028 since early 4Q26, resulting in a slight slowdown in overall DRAM procurement momentum. 
This growing caution stems from concerns that the outcome of the U.S. midterm elections could affect the pace of future data center development, potential changes to NVIDIA's financing policies for neocloud providers, and geopolitical restrictions affecting the flow of advanced-node chips and access to leased computing resources.Given the uncertainty surrounding the extent to which these developments will affect demand, TrendForce has outlined two scenarios—a base case and a bear case—for DRAM contract price trends over the next two years. 
Under the base case, conventional DRAM contract price increases are expected to narrow progressively throughout 2027, with prices potentially leveling off in the second half of the year before declining in 2028.
The base case takes several demand-side factors into account. Consumer electronics manufacturers are facing mounting sales pressure and have limited capacity to absorb further price increases. articles.title: Andorra aprobó una ley que prohíbe a los menores de 16 años usar ciertas redes sociales
articles.summary:
El Consejo General de Andorra, el Parlamento del país, aprobó el 26 de noviembre una reforma de la ley de derechos de niños y adolescentes que prohíbe a los menores de 16 años acceder a determinadas redes sociales. Todos los grupos la apoyaron, salvo Andorra Endavant, que se abstuvo.
La restricción no alcanza a todas las plataformas. Según La Veu Lliure, medio digital del país europeo, el texto se refiere a ciertas plataformas y no a una prohibición general. El ministro de Transformación Digital y Función Pública, Marc Rossell, afirmó en el debate que “esta no es una ley de prohibiciones” y que busca garantizar los derechos de la infancia en el entorno digital.
Además de la restricción de edad, la norma reconoce el derecho de los menores a la desconexión digital, refuerza la protección de su identidad digital y obliga a poner a disposición de familias y centros educativos herramientas gratuitas de control parental.
Rossell citó el último estudio de Unicef: los niños reciben su primer teléfono a los 10,5 años de media, más del 90% de los jóvenes dice estar registrado en al menos una red social y uno de cada cuatro adolescentes afirma haber visto pornografía antes de los 12.

La reforma llegó al Parlamento tras el proyecto que el Gobierno andorrano aprobó en marzo. Según la cobertura de ese momento del medio andorrano Alto, el texto exige un sistema “robusto” de verificación de edad para impedir que los menores usen datos falsos y b…

articles.title: Un ingeniero químico muestra cómo limpiar el inodoro de forma correcta: “Te voy a mostrar lo que he aprendido sobre cómo limpiar correctamente el inodoro”
articles.summary:
Si eres de los que echa un buen chorro de lejía al inodoro y después pasa la escobilla, puede que estés saltándote un paso importante. Diego, un ingeniero químico que comparte consejos en Instagram (@renovandoconideas), ha explicado cómo limpiar el váter y por qué utilizar más productos no significa conseguir una limpieza mejor.
En realidad, lo primero que recomienda es bastante sencillo: retirar la suciedad visible antes de desinfectar. Así lo explica también el artículo publicado por Clarín, que recoge sus consejos y las indicaciones de los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) de Estados Unidos.
El error de mezclar productos para limpiar el váter
Para empezar, utiliza un limpiador adecuado para el baño y frota las zonas donde haya suciedad. Después tendrás que aclarar los restos del producto siguiendo sus instrucciones. Si necesitas desinfectar, aplica un desinfectante compatible con la superficie y respeta el tiempo que indica el fabricante. No sirve de mucho retirarlo antes de que haya actuado.
Pero hay una advertencia especialmente importante: nunca mezcles lejía con vinagre, amoniaco ni otros limpiadores. Algunas combinaciones pueden desprender gases tóxicos, así que tampoco conviene echar lejía directamente en un inodoro donde todavía quedan restos de otro producto. Además, es recomendable mantener el baño ventilado mientras limpias.

articles.title: Tamer Bahgat is betting on social commerce in Nigeria
articles.summary:
For nearly two decades, Tamer Bahgat built a career in international finance, moving between New York, London, Dubai, and Singapore. He worked as a finance and private equity lawyer, became a partner at London Magic Circle firms, and previously worked as a banker at Goldman Sachs. Three years ago, he left that career behind to build a technology company in Nigeria.
The idea for the venture had taken shape about 14 years earlier during his exposure to Asia’s technology industry. Bahgat told TechCabal in November that he became interested in how tech companies in the region were building digital ecosystems that brought different services together. He said he believed the model could be adapted for African markets, where growing digital adoption presented an opportunity to rethink how people accessed everyday services.
“When I experienced what they were doing in technology, how they were building it, what their future looked like, and compared it to what we were seeing in the Western world, I came to the conclusion that, given the infrastructure we have across the continent, given its size, its regulators, its culture, its people, a tried and tested model in that shape should be really where the inspiration comes from, and not so much the Western cultures,” he told TechCabal.

articles.title: Aragón pierde otro centro de datos: Capital Energy se retira de Épila y vende su conexión eléctrica a Blackstone
articles.summary:
Aragón se ha convertido en uno de los territorios más atractivos para la industria de los centros de datos. Pero no todos los proyectos anunciados llegan a construirse. De hecho, la región ha perdido recientemente otro megacampus de centros de datos. En este caso, se trataba de Epilon, el campus que Box2Bit iba a construir en Épila, (Zaragoza). Con esta retirada, son tres ya los proyectos de este tipo que la compañía abandona en la región.
En esta “espantada”, Bit2Box, además, ha vendido a Blackstone los derechos asociados a 150 MW de capacidad de conexión eléctrica que había conseguido para Epilon y que ya no le van a hacer falta. El fondo de inversiones, por su lado, aprovechará esta potencia para reforzar su proyecto Rhodes, en Calatorao. Y es que los centros de datos requieren de un suministro eléctrico continuo y tan potente que la energía es ahora el bien más preciado para las empresas tecnológicas.
Un proyecto más que no se va a desarrollar. Según el portal Data Center Dynamics, Box2Bit anunció en su día tres campus de centros de datos en Aragón, pero, a día de hoy, ninguno seguirá adelante. Primero fue el Campus Ebro en Cariñena, valorado en 3.400 millones de euros, que fue descartado al quedarse fuera del plan de inversiones del Ministerio para los próximos cinco años. El segundo fue La Charluca, en Calatayud, que no consiguió obtener acceso a la red de transmisión y que tampoco llegó a desarrollarse.

articles.title: New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info
articles.summary:
Medical technology company Boston Scientific is sending data breach notices to individuals affected by a cyberattack on the firm.
According to a notification sample Boston Scientific shared with U.S. authorities, the hacker used social engineering in a voice phishing (vishing) attack to gain access to the company's cloud infrastructure.
The attack exposed cloud-based applications and cloud-hosted data between May 7 and 1.
The company became aware of the unauthorized access on May 12, and the investigation determined that a data breach occurred on November 5.
Individuals in multiple U.S. states have been impacted, exposing personal details and medical information. According to the Texas Attorney General breach portal, the incident exposed information from 117,789 people, which included:
- Full name
- Physical address
- Social Security Number (SSN)
- Government-issued ID number (e.g., passport, state ID card)
- Medical information
- Health insurance information
- Date of birth
The letter sent to impacted individuals specifies that patient medical records and data from remote monitoring systems, connected medical devices, and clinical case management or workflow applications were not exposed.
Boston Scientific is a Massachusetts-based medical device maker whose products include stents, catheters, pacemakers, defibrillators, and endoscopes.

articles.title: Unpatched Cacti zero-day with public PoC gives remote code execution
articles.summary:
A zero-day vulnerability in the Cacti network monitoring platform has been publicly disclosed, along with a proof-of-concept exploit that lets unauthenticated attackers execute commands on vulnerable servers.
The exploit, dubbed "4HTTP2SHELL" (previously 4HTTP2ROOT), was published on Thanksgiving Day by a cybersecurity researcher known as ek0ms savi0r from the Church of Malware, who demonstrated how the vulnerability can be exploited using just four HTTP requests.
Cacti is an open-source network monitoring and graphing tool used to monitor the performance of servers, routers, switches, firewalls, and other network infrastructure.
Because the software can store credentials and SNMP passphrases used to access or read data from monitored devices, compromising a Cacti server could potentially give attackers access to other systems on a corporate network.
The researcher published a technical write-up, a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, and a video demonstrating the attack in a GitHub repository named "Sad Girls 0day Club."
"I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server user in four requests. No login. No valid API key. No phishing. Just four HTTP requests against the default guest surface," explains the researcher.
The vulnerability stems from weak input validation that allows an unauthenticated attacker to inject SQL statements into the application's database and modify commands executed by Cacti's real-time poller.

articles.title: Rockstar Games : les salariés du studio de GTA 6 rejettent la reconnaissance syndicale
articles.summary:
Les salariés de Rockstar Games au Royaume-Uni étaient appelés à voter pour la reconnaissance formelle d'un syndicat. La réponse a été cinglante.
Les employés de Rockstar Games au Royaume-Uni se sont prononcés à une large majorité contre la reconnaissance formelle du syndicat IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union. Le scrutin s'est déroulé au même moment où l'entreprise a sorti Grand Theft Auto 6, qui a généré 3,79 milliards de dollars de précommandes et de ventes dès son premier jour.
Un scrutin à forte participation
Il y a des scrutins à la participation élevée, et c'est le cas ici. Plus de 93 % des salariés des bureaux d'Édimbourg, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee et Londres ont participé à ce vote, organisé sur deux semaines. D'après les chiffres rapportés par IGN, 1 163 d'entre eux ont voté contre la reconnaissance formelle de cette branche de l'IWGB (Independent Workers Union of Great Britain), contre 381 qui y étaient favorables.
Mais alors, que veut dire ce résultat concrètement ? C'est simple, la direction de Rockstar n'a pas l'obligation de reconnaître officiellement le syndicat, ni de tenir des réunions avec ses représentants, ce dernier n'étant pas officiel. Le syndicat indique toutefois qu'il continuera à s'organiser sans accord formel avec l'entreprise.

articles.title: Voler une Tesla dans GTA 6 est une très mauvaise idée, voici pourquoi
articles.summary:
Tout le sel de la licence Grand Theft Auto repose sur le vol de voiture. On ne peut pas faire plus explicite comme titre de franchise ! Choisir un véhicule au détour d’une rue, dégager son conducteur et prendre le volant est une des mécaniques centrales du jeu depuis le premier opus sorti en 1997. Six épisodes plus tard, le processus n’a pas réellement changé, même si Rockstar a glissé une petite sournoiserie concernant un modèle en particulier.
Copie sans détour de la Tesla Model S, la Coil Raiden n’hésitera pas à vous mettre des bâtons dans les roues. Bien sûr, cela est déjà le cas avec d’autres véhicules. Les plus récents sont par exemple équipés d’une clé mains-libres qu’il est nécessaire de hacker pour pouvoir réellement démarrer la voiture. Parfois, vous aurez même un chat qui essaiera de vous attaquer pendant que vous conduisez une voiture fraîchement volée !
La Coil Raiden prend le contrôle et vous piège
Des obstacles amusants, mais pas forcément très impressionnants. Sur la Coil Raiden, le délire atteint un tout autre niveau puisqu’après avoir éjecté le propriétaire, vous n’irez pas bien loin. Enfin, si, mais pas de votre propre volonté… La voiture fermera en effet ses vitres et conduira à votre place, comme si le FSD avait pris le contrôle du véhicule. Sauf que le FSD est évidemment désactivable dans la vraie vie, ce qui n’est pas le cas dans GTA 6.
